correctness.rationale: Ordinary strict path homomorphisms satisfy |f(i+1)−f(i)|=1. For an idempotent f, its image must be an interval [b,b+k−1], k≥2, and every image vertex is fixed, hence f is exactly a retraction. The exterior domain tails of lengths a and d−a are independent nearest-neighbor walks from respective target endpoints, yielding I_nk=∑_a w_k(a)w_k(d−a), d=n−k; reversal conjugation fixes exactly centered intervals (d even) with a single left-tail choice, S_nk=w_k(d/2), else zero. Burnside gives orbit sizes, and geometric series yield W_k(z)^2/W_k(z²) resolvents. For k>d, half-line ballot enumeration yields stabilized binomials and n>2d exact cutoff. Independently enumerated strict homomorphisms, composed maps to test idempotence and reversal for n=2..11 (total counts 1,3,6,12,21,40,69,130,226,423); all agree. Finite tests not proof of all n.
residual_risks: Infinite theorem not derived from finite checks; reconstructed written proof supplies its generality.
